description: Set the standing rules of how this coach works, applied to every athlete on the roster — "no intensity on Mondays", "never two hard days back to back", "long ride Saturday unless someone is racing". They travel with every get_plan, so a rule is written once instead of repeated in each athlete's notes. Send both forms: `rules` is the prose a planner is briefed with, and `rules_json` is the same standing rules as typed objects, which audit_plan and create_workouts check every week against and report as findings. A rule only in the prose is advice; a rule in rules_json is enforced. Anything the vocabulary cannot say stays in the prose. Read tripeak://guide/house-rules for the vocabulary, and note that both fields are replaced whole — read the current ones from get_account first and send them back with the change folded in.

rules.description: The complete rules, in plain prose. Empty string clears them.

rules_json.description: The same standing rules as checkable objects. Each is {rule, …fields}, where rule is one of: no_quality_on, no_sessions_on, min_days_between_quality, max_sessions_per_day, weekly_sport_minimum, weekly_quality_minimum (at least N quality sessions of a sport in a week), min_session_distance (every session of a sport at least N metres), weekly_hours_max, long_session_on, rest_day_on. Fields: days (lower-case weekday names), sport, count, plus optional because (repeated back to whoever breaks the rule), severity (high/medium/low) and unless (["race_week"]). Invalid rules are rejected with every problem listed at once. Omit the field to leave the stored ones alone; send [] to clear them. e.g. [{"rule":"no_quality_on","days":["monday"],"because":"most of them work Mondays"},{"rule":"min_days_between_quality","count":2},{"rule":"long_session_on","sport":"bike","days":["saturday"],"unless":["race_week"]}]

name: set_coaching_rules
